author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **6.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- In 6.0, the coverage.py exceptions moved from coverage.misc to
  coverage.exceptions. These exceptions are not part of the public supported
  API, CoverageException is. But a number of other third-party packages were
  importing the exceptions from coverage.misc, so they are now available from
  there again (`issue 1226`_).

- Changed an internal detail of how tomli is imported, so that tomli can use
  coverage.py for their own test suite (`issue 1228`_).

- Defend against an obscure possibility under code obfuscation, where a
  function can have an argument called "self", but no local named "self"
  (`pull request 1210`_).  Thanks, Ben Carlsson.

.. _pull request 1210: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1210
.. _issue 1226: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1226
.. _issue 1228: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1228


.. _changes_60:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage html`` command now prints a message indicating where the HTML
  report was written.  Fixes `issue 1195`_.

- The ``coverage combine`` command now prints messages indicating each data
  file being combined.  Fixes `issue 1105`_.

- The HTML report now includes a sentence about skipped files due to
  ``skip_covered`` or ``skip_empty`` settings.  Fixes `issue 1163`_.

- Unrecognized options in the configuration file are no longer errors. They are
  now warnings, to ease the use of coverage across versions.  Fixes `issue
  1035`_.

- Fix handling of exceptions through context managers in Python 3.10. A missing
  exception is no longer considered a missing branch from the with statement.
  Fixes `issue 1205`_.

- Fix another rarer instance of "Error binding parameter 0 - probably
  unsupported type." (`issue 1010`_).

- Creating a directory for the coverage data file now is safer against
  conflicts when two coverage runs happen simultaneously (`pull 1220`_).
  Thanks, Clément Pit-Claudel.

.. _issue 1035: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1035
.. _issue 1105: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1105
.. _issue 1163: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1163
.. _issue 1195: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1195
.. _issue 1205: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1205
.. _pull 1220: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1220


.. _changes_60b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 2.7, PyPy 2, and Python 3.5.

- Added support for the Python 3.10 ``match/case`` syntax.

- Data collection is now thread-safe.  There may have been rare instances of
  exceptions raised in multi-threaded programs.

- Plugins (like the `Django coverage plugin`_) were generating "Already
  imported a file that will be measured" warnings about Django itself.  These
  have been fixed, closing `issue 1150`_.

- Warnings generated by coverage.py are now real Python warnings.

- Using ``--fail-under=100`` with coverage near 100% could result in the
  self-contradictory message :code:`total of 100 is less than fail-under=100`.
  This bug (`issue 1168`_) is now fixed.

- The ``COVERAGE_DEBUG_FILE`` environment variable now accepts ``stdout`` and
  ``stderr`` to write to those destinations.

- TOML parsing now uses the `tomli`_ library.

- Some minor changes to usually invisible details of the HTML report:

  - Use a modern hash algorithm when fingerprinting, for high-security
    environments (`issue 1189`_).  When generating the HTML report, we save the
    hash of the data, to avoid regenerating an unchanged HTML page. We used to
    use MD5 to generate the hash, and now use SHA-3-256.  This was never a
    security concern, but security scanners would notice the MD5 algorithm and
    raise a false alarm.

  - Change how report file names are generated, to avoid leading underscores
    (`issue 1167`_), to avoid rare file name collisions (`issue 584`_), and to
    avoid file names becoming too long (`issue 580`_).

.. _Django coverage plugin: https://pypi.org/project/django-coverage-plugin/
.. _issue 580: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/580
.. _issue 584: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/584
.. _issue 1150: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1150
.. _issue 1167: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1167
.. _issue 1168: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1168
.. _issue 1189: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1189
.. _tomli: https://pypi.org/project/tomli/


.. _changes_56b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.6b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

Note: 5.6 final was never released. These changes are part of 6.0.

- Third-party packages are now ignored in coverage reporting.  This solves a
  few problems:

  - Coverage will no longer report about other people's code (`issue 876`_).
    This is true even when using ``--source=.`` with a venv in the current
    directory.

  - Coverage will no longer generate "Already imported a file that will be
    measured" warnings about coverage itself (`issue 905`_).

- The HTML report uses j/k to move up and down among the highlighted chunks of
  code.  They used to highlight the current chunk, but 5.0 broke that behavior.
  Now the highlighting is working again.

- The JSON report now includes ``percent_covered_display``, a string with the
  total percentage, rounded to the same number of decimal places as the other
  reports' totals.

.. _issue 876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/876
.. _issue 905: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/905


.. _changes_55:
   ```
   
  
</details>

  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/coverage
  - Changelog: https://pyup.io/changelogs/coverage/
  - Repo: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy

author: bentley
body:
Wikipedia:

> The mark is made using ‘a pair of apostrophes’;<sup>[1]</sup> ‘a pair of marks " used underneath a word’;<sup>[3]</sup> the symbol " (quotation mark);<sup>[2][4]</sup> or the symbol ” (right double quotation mark).<sup>[5]</sup>

Notably missing from that description is U+3003 〃. In fact, U+3003 is part of Unicode’s [CJK Symbols and Punctuation block](https://unicode.org/charts/PDF/U3000.pdf). This is why it looks far too big in English text—it’s sized to fit in with ｆｕｌｌｗｉｄｔｈ　ｌｅｔｔｅｒｓ and Han characters. It’s also double‐width in a terminal.

I replaced it with two rsquo (`’’`), although I’m not sure whether it makes any real difference to just use rdquo (`”`).

author: sisou
body:
When messages arrive very quickly after each other, or the message handler is waiting for the `Blob.arraybuffer` to resolve (it's async), it can happen that another message that arrived in parallel resolves the promise already, losing the first message.

This commit introduces a payload queue, in which payloads that take longer are stored, and taken out on the next iteration.

**Attention: The drawback of the current implementation is that the queue is only processed when a new message arrives.**

author: romainmuller
body:
The construct framework detection logic caused packages to fail
ingesting when they declared a range dependency on the construct
framework package (as opposed to a version-pinned dependency).
This changes the logic to parse the ranges and select the minimum
supported major version instead, which corrects the issue.

Additionally, the framework detection only looked into dependencies,
meaning that the framework packages themselves (i.e: `@aws-cdk/core`)
did not get a framework identified. This is now fixed.

Fixes #376

author: robertknight
body:
**Depends on https://github.com/hypothesis/client/pull/3807**

Change how the sidebar is notified of guest frames being unloaded to
support guest frames where the client has been loaded via means other
than `HypothesisInjector` or where the guest is cross-origin.

Instead of listening for the guest frame's 'unload' event from the
parent frame in `HypothesisInjector`, the guest frame instead listens
for this event itself and sends a `hypothesisGuestUnloaded` message to
the host frame via `window.postMessage`, which in turn is handled in the
`Sidebar` class to relay it to the sidebar app via a `destroyFrame` RPC
call. This indirect route works around a bug in Safari (see code
comments).

As well as supporting future use cases, this also simplifies the
`HypothesisInjector` class as it no longer needs access to the `Bridge`.

To facilitate testing, I changed the http://localhost:3000/document/parent-frame page to add a "Toggle frame" button that removes or adds the iframe to the page.

----

**Testing:**

1. Go to http://localhost:3000/document/parent-frame
2. Add annotations to the iframe
3. Click the Toggle button to remove the frame from the page, then again to re-add it

When the frame is removed the annotations should disappear from the sidebar, and when they are re-added, they should re-appear again. They _may_ show up as Orphans when loaded, but this is due to an existing issue unrelated to these changes.

Additionally if you combine this branch with https://github.com/hypothesis/client/pull/3811, you'll see the list of URLs in the Help panel's "About this version" tab update to reflect the connected frames when you toggle the presence of the guest frame.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.4** to **6.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- In 6.0, the coverage.py exceptions moved from coverage.misc to
  coverage.exceptions. These exceptions are not part of the public supported
  API, CoverageException is. But a number of other third-party packages were
  importing the exceptions from coverage.misc, so they are now available from
  there again (`issue 1226`_).

- Changed an internal detail of how tomli is imported, so that tomli can use
  coverage.py for their own test suite (`issue 1228`_).

- Defend against an obscure possibility under code obfuscation, where a
  function can have an argument called "self", but no local named "self"
  (`pull request 1210`_).  Thanks, Ben Carlsson.

.. _pull request 1210: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1210
.. _issue 1226: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1226
.. _issue 1228: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1228


.. _changes_60:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage html`` command now prints a message indicating where the HTML
  report was written.  Fixes `issue 1195`_.

- The ``coverage combine`` command now prints messages indicating each data
  file being combined.  Fixes `issue 1105`_.

- The HTML report now includes a sentence about skipped files due to
  ``skip_covered`` or ``skip_empty`` settings.  Fixes `issue 1163`_.

- Unrecognized options in the configuration file are no longer errors. They are
  now warnings, to ease the use of coverage across versions.  Fixes `issue
  1035`_.

- Fix handling of exceptions through context managers in Python 3.10. A missing
  exception is no longer considered a missing branch from the with statement.
  Fixes `issue 1205`_.

- Fix another rarer instance of "Error binding parameter 0 - probably
  unsupported type." (`issue 1010`_).

- Creating a directory for the coverage data file now is safer against
  conflicts when two coverage runs happen simultaneously (`pull 1220`_).
  Thanks, Clément Pit-Claudel.

.. _issue 1035: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1035
.. _issue 1105: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1105
.. _issue 1163: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1163
.. _issue 1195: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1195
.. _issue 1205: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1205
.. _pull 1220: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1220


.. _changes_60b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 2.7, PyPy 2, and Python 3.5.

- Added support for the Python 3.10 ``match/case`` syntax.

- Data collection is now thread-safe.  There may have been rare instances of
  exceptions raised in multi-threaded programs.

- Plugins (like the `Django coverage plugin`_) were generating "Already
  imported a file that will be measured" warnings about Django itself.  These
  have been fixed, closing `issue 1150`_.

- Warnings generated by coverage.py are now real Python warnings.

- Using ``--fail-under=100`` with coverage near 100% could result in the
  self-contradictory message :code:`total of 100 is less than fail-under=100`.
  This bug (`issue 1168`_) is now fixed.

- The ``COVERAGE_DEBUG_FILE`` environment variable now accepts ``stdout`` and
  ``stderr`` to write to those destinations.

- TOML parsing now uses the `tomli`_ library.

- Some minor changes to usually invisible details of the HTML report:

  - Use a modern hash algorithm when fingerprinting, for high-security
    environments (`issue 1189`_).  When generating the HTML report, we save the
    hash of the data, to avoid regenerating an unchanged HTML page. We used to
    use MD5 to generate the hash, and now use SHA-3-256.  This was never a
    security concern, but security scanners would notice the MD5 algorithm and
    raise a false alarm.

  - Change how report file names are generated, to avoid leading underscores
    (`issue 1167`_), to avoid rare file name collisions (`issue 584`_), and to
    avoid file names becoming too long (`issue 580`_).

.. _Django coverage plugin: https://pypi.org/project/django-coverage-plugin/
.. _issue 580: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/580
.. _issue 584: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/584
.. _issue 1150: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1150
.. _issue 1167: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1167
.. _issue 1168: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1168
.. _issue 1189: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1189
.. _tomli: https://pypi.org/project/tomli/


.. _changes_56b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.6b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

Note: 5.6 final was never released. These changes are part of 6.0.

- Third-party packages are now ignored in coverage reporting.  This solves a
  few problems:

  - Coverage will no longer report about other people's code (`issue 876`_).
    This is true even when using ``--source=.`` with a venv in the current
    directory.

  - Coverage will no longer generate "Already imported a file that will be
    measured" warnings about coverage itself (`issue 905`_).

- The HTML report uses j/k to move up and down among the highlighted chunks of
  code.  They used to highlight the current chunk, but 5.0 broke that behavior.
  Now the highlighting is working again.

- The JSON report now includes ``percent_covered_display``, a string with the
  total percentage, rounded to the same number of decimal places as the other
  reports' totals.

.. _issue 876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/876
.. _issue 905: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/905


.. _changes_55:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- ``coverage combine`` has a new option, ``--keep`` to keep the original data
  files after combining them.  The default is still to delete the files after
  they have been combined.  This was requested in `issue 1108`_ and implemented
  in `pull request 1110`_.  Thanks, Éric Larivière.

- When reporting missing branches in ``coverage report``, branches aren't
  reported that jump to missing lines.  This adds to the long-standing behavior
  of not reporting branches from missing lines.  Now branches are only reported
  if both the source and destination lines are executed.  Closes both `issue
  1065`_ and `issue 955`_.

- Minor improvements to the HTML report:

  - The state of the line visibility selector buttons is saved in local storage
    so you don't have to fiddle with them so often, fixing `issue 1123`_.

  - It has a little more room for line numbers so that 4-digit numbers work
    well, fixing `issue 1124`_.

- Improved the error message when combining line and branch data, so that users
  will be more likely to understand what's happening, closing `issue 803`_.

.. _issue 803: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/803
.. _issue 955: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/955
.. _issue 1065: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1065
.. _issue 1108: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1108
.. _pull request 1110: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1110
.. _issue 1123: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1123
.. _issue 1124: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1124


.. _changes_54:
   ```
   
  
</details>

  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/coverage
  - Changelog: https://pyup.io/changelogs/coverage/

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.1** to **6.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- In 6.0, the coverage.py exceptions moved from coverage.misc to
  coverage.exceptions. These exceptions are not part of the public supported
  API, CoverageException is. But a number of other third-party packages were
  importing the exceptions from coverage.misc, so they are now available from
  there again (`issue 1226`_).

- Changed an internal detail of how tomli is imported, so that tomli can use
  coverage.py for their own test suite (`issue 1228`_).

- Defend against an obscure possibility under code obfuscation, where a
  function can have an argument called "self", but no local named "self"
  (`pull request 1210`_).  Thanks, Ben Carlsson.

.. _pull request 1210: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1210
.. _issue 1226: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1226
.. _issue 1228: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1228


.. _changes_60:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage html`` command now prints a message indicating where the HTML
  report was written.  Fixes `issue 1195`_.

- The ``coverage combine`` command now prints messages indicating each data
  file being combined.  Fixes `issue 1105`_.

- The HTML report now includes a sentence about skipped files due to
  ``skip_covered`` or ``skip_empty`` settings.  Fixes `issue 1163`_.

- Unrecognized options in the configuration file are no longer errors. They are
  now warnings, to ease the use of coverage across versions.  Fixes `issue
  1035`_.

- Fix handling of exceptions through context managers in Python 3.10. A missing
  exception is no longer considered a missing branch from the with statement.
  Fixes `issue 1205`_.

- Fix another rarer instance of "Error binding parameter 0 - probably
  unsupported type." (`issue 1010`_).

- Creating a directory for the coverage data file now is safer against
  conflicts when two coverage runs happen simultaneously (`pull 1220`_).
  Thanks, Clément Pit-Claudel.

.. _issue 1035: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1035
.. _issue 1105: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1105
.. _issue 1163: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1163
.. _issue 1195: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1195
.. _issue 1205: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1205
.. _pull 1220: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1220


.. _changes_60b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 2.7, PyPy 2, and Python 3.5.

- Added support for the Python 3.10 ``match/case`` syntax.

- Data collection is now thread-safe.  There may have been rare instances of
  exceptions raised in multi-threaded programs.

- Plugins (like the `Django coverage plugin`_) were generating "Already
  imported a file that will be measured" warnings about Django itself.  These
  have been fixed, closing `issue 1150`_.

- Warnings generated by coverage.py are now real Python warnings.

- Using ``--fail-under=100`` with coverage near 100% could result in the
  self-contradictory message :code:`total of 100 is less than fail-under=100`.
  This bug (`issue 1168`_) is now fixed.

- The ``COVERAGE_DEBUG_FILE`` environment variable now accepts ``stdout`` and
  ``stderr`` to write to those destinations.

- TOML parsing now uses the `tomli`_ library.

- Some minor changes to usually invisible details of the HTML report:

  - Use a modern hash algorithm when fingerprinting, for high-security
    environments (`issue 1189`_).  When generating the HTML report, we save the
    hash of the data, to avoid regenerating an unchanged HTML page. We used to
    use MD5 to generate the hash, and now use SHA-3-256.  This was never a
    security concern, but security scanners would notice the MD5 algorithm and
    raise a false alarm.

  - Change how report file names are generated, to avoid leading underscores
    (`issue 1167`_), to avoid rare file name collisions (`issue 584`_), and to
    avoid file names becoming too long (`issue 580`_).

.. _Django coverage plugin: https://pypi.org/project/django-coverage-plugin/
.. _issue 580: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/580
.. _issue 584: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/584
.. _issue 1150: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1150
.. _issue 1167: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1167
.. _issue 1168: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1168
.. _issue 1189: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1189
.. _tomli: https://pypi.org/project/tomli/


.. _changes_56b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.6b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

Note: 5.6 final was never released. These changes are part of 6.0.

- Third-party packages are now ignored in coverage reporting.  This solves a
  few problems:

  - Coverage will no longer report about other people's code (`issue 876`_).
    This is true even when using ``--source=.`` with a venv in the current
    directory.

  - Coverage will no longer generate "Already imported a file that will be
    measured" warnings about coverage itself (`issue 905`_).

- The HTML report uses j/k to move up and down among the highlighted chunks of
  code.  They used to highlight the current chunk, but 5.0 broke that behavior.
  Now the highlighting is working again.

- The JSON report now includes ``percent_covered_display``, a string with the
  total percentage, rounded to the same number of decimal places as the other
  reports' totals.

.. _issue 876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/876
.. _issue 905: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/905


.. _changes_55:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- ``coverage combine`` has a new option, ``--keep`` to keep the original data
  files after combining them.  The default is still to delete the files after
  they have been combined.  This was requested in `issue 1108`_ and implemented
  in `pull request 1110`_.  Thanks, Éric Larivière.

- When reporting missing branches in ``coverage report``, branches aren't
  reported that jump to missing lines.  This adds to the long-standing behavior
  of not reporting branches from missing lines.  Now branches are only reported
  if both the source and destination lines are executed.  Closes both `issue
  1065`_ and `issue 955`_.

- Minor improvements to the HTML report:

  - The state of the line visibility selector buttons is saved in local storage
    so you don't have to fiddle with them so often, fixing `issue 1123`_.

  - It has a little more room for line numbers so that 4-digit numbers work
    well, fixing `issue 1124`_.

- Improved the error message when combining line and branch data, so that users
  will be more likely to understand what's happening, closing `issue 803`_.

.. _issue 803: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/803
.. _issue 955: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/955
.. _issue 1065: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1065
.. _issue 1108: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1108
.. _pull request 1110: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1110
.. _issue 1123: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1123
.. _issue 1124: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1124


.. _changes_54:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- The text report produced by ``coverage report`` now always outputs a TOTAL

author: benwtrent
body:
This commit adds the new `normalize_above` parameter to the `p_value` significant
terms heuristic.

This parameter allows for consistent significance results at various scales. When a total count (in or out of the set background set) is above the `normalize_above` parameter, both the total set and the set including the term are scaled by `normalize_above/count` where count is term in the set or total set size.

Since the `Timestamp` component displays the provided timestamp based on the user timezone by default, we do not need the `UserTimezone` component.
The only difference, when a user has no timezone configured, we are the `Timestamp` component will use the browser timezone as a fallback.

author: undermaken
body:
## Short description
This PR fixes a bug that causes:
no push notifications when the session is not more valid and then the user runs the app the first time.

All those that start after the first one, the push notifications come working back again

The bug is due to a race condition: the PN token is deleted after it can be renew again

### how it works - before
![current implementation](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/822471/136408781-a211c738-0e42-4c21-a638-7f63492470bb.png)

### how the bug happens - before
This happens because we have to control over the exact sequence of actions: delete and renew of PN token
The right order must be:

1. delete
2. renew

but almost all the times is

1. renew
2. delete

![current implementation - bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/822471/136408945-f2e45a80-467b-467c-9d29-e556cf56f0b8.png)

------

### how it works - now
![New implementation - no - bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/822471/136409520-89a5f2ea-14cd-47cf-a53d-30442de11b4b.png)



### how the bug does NOT happen - now
![New implementation - bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/822471/136441309-47ca38c2-f6ea-4114-bdb5-13ecb743edfb.png)



## how to reproduce the bug
- install the current version of the app `1.35.0.1` from the store
- do login
- send a message to your profile
- push notification will be received
- do login on another devices or using web
- come back to your device
- session is expired
- send a message to your profile
- push notification WONT be received (this is right)
- do login
- send a message to your profile
- push notification WONT be received 🐛 

## how to test
- use this code to install a build that can receive PN to your device
or
- use [this APK](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZY0AEv8VJZ0GtW8_8oUTbV5Asdf9RLmz/view?usp=sharing) based on the code of this PR

author: patrickracicot
body:
### WHY are these changes introduced? Fixes #4419 The goal of this PR is to address the accessibility issue concerning the `ActionList` component used inside the `Popover` component.. Screen readers are unable to find, navigate into and trigger actions in the revealed content. ### WHAT is this pull request doing? In this proposal, we enhance the `ActionList` to be [WAI-Aria compliant](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-practices-1.1/examples/menu-button/menu-button-actions.html). #### **Navigation** To do so we start by properly support arrow (⬆️ & ⬇️ ) navigation as well as navigation wrap (which consist of bringing the focus from first to last and last to first action item instead of leaving the content context on arrow navigation). #### **Role attribution** We also enhance the `ActionList` component usage of the `actionRole` prop. If a consumer sets this prop to the value `menuitem`, the component `ActionList`, `Section` and `Item` will automatically set the proper `menu` and `menuitem` roles. #### **On-open Focus** In order to have the screen readers properly announce the context to the user, we are adding `tabIndex="-1"` to the root `
    ` element. This will ensure that `autoFocusTarget="first-node"` will set the focus to this root `
      ` element which will in-turn allow the screen reader to properly announce to the user that the context is now on a list. In the case of **multi-section**, the tabIndex and menu role needs to be assigned on the `
        ` rendered in the `Actionlist` component. https://github.com/Shopify/polaris-react/blob/c463b45e226fa6ea90e91ddc825a8fc48ecaf352/src/components/ActionList/ActionList.tsx#L96-L106 While also making sure that we assign the `presentation` role to sub-section `

-----

Our `brew vendor-gems` command mostly does not require any gem dependencies. The one exception to this was the GPG setup step, which invokes formula loading and the large amount of code involved in that.

This actually causes problems like what is seen in https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/12195/checks?check_run_id=3826077427#step:7:313.

There's two solutions for this:

* Allow `brew vendor-gems` to use external dependencies after installation by adding a full `$LOAD_PATH` reload.
* Just remove formula loading since it's not really necessary.

I just did the latter as it's substantially cheaper, and easier to implement.

author: github-learning-lab[bot]
body:
## Triggering GitHub Apps Actions that a person or tool takes on GitHub can be used to trigger events. Creating an issue, making a commit, or leaving a comment, to name a few, are logged on GitHub. If GitHub doesn't use it, it can still be useful to other applications. When you install an app, you give the app permission to receive some of this data from GitHub. That data allows the apps to react in ways that are useful to you. You can also allow the app to send information back, or change information completely. It's important to mention that GitHub Apps are not people. You can't interact with them by doing things like using an @mention, or assigning them to review your work. On the other hand, they can do things that humans can't - like crunch big data, piece together networks of information and find bugs or errors that people wouldn't. ## App components An app is like a home security system. It's equipped to watch your house at all times, but only notifies you for specific criteria. When you install a home security system, you need to worry about a few components: - **Electricity** to have the power to run continuously. You don't want failure when you aren't watching. - **Standard behaviors** to detect things like movement, noise, and doors opening. You don't want to have to program it to understand these actions -- you want to select how it responds to them. - A **location** that will be watched. - A **notification delivery service** -- either to your phone, a dedicated security service, or both. Just like a home security system, a GitHub App only watches for specific actions, and then responds in predetermined ways. ## Step 2: Trigger the WIP app **WIP** is a common abbreviation to mean **work in progress**. The app you've just installed is concerned with one action: changing the title of a pull request. Let's test it out and see what the result is by updating the title of this pull request. ### :keyboard: Activity: Test the app by editing the pull request title 1. To the right of the pull request title, click the **Edit** button 1. Add `WIP` to the beginning of the title 1. Click **Save**

author: lukehesluke
body:
Closes https://github.com/openactive/openactive-test-suite/issues/460

What this PR does:

* Create AssertOpportunityFlowStage, which can be used to check that Opportunities in an Order have the right capacity (using functionality created in Broker in https://github.com/openactive/openactive-test-suite/pull/461)
* Create FlowStageRun class, which can be used to group a "run" of FlowStages together. It's handy because it allows you to add other stages to a "run" without having to explicitly add each of those stages to every test. This is used in this PR. Most of the tests that have
  ```js
  FlowStageUtils.describeRunAndCheckIsSuccessfulAndValid(c1);
  FlowStageUtils.describeRunAndCheckIsSuccessfulAndValid(c2);
  ```
  Are unchanged, but, under the hood, `c1` has changed from having type `C1FlowStage` to having type `FlowStageRun<{ c1: C1FlowStage, assertOpportunityCapacityAfterC1: AssertOpportunityCapacityFlowStage }>`. Both of these stages will be run and checked.
* Updated existing recipes (e.g. `FlowStageRecipes.initialiseSimpleC1C2Flow`) to automatically use capacity checks after each of C1, C2 & book.
* Added some new cancellation recipes like `FlowStageRecipes.runs.customerCancel.successfulCancelAssertOrderUpdateAndCapacity`. All cancellation tests now use these, which means that they all test capacity.
* More complicated capacity checks for:
  * amending-order-quote tests - Check that Opportunities which have been switched out of an Order have their capacities restored (as leases should be dropped)
  * leasing tests - Align capacity assertions with the batching nature of these tests.

Fixes an issue that we sometimes show `Error: Error: <message>` in the error banner. Also makes error handling more uniform in a few places.

* Address error cleanup TODO in auth_service.ts
* Have the RPC service throw real errors instead of strings with an `"Error: "` prefix. The stringified version is still the same, since `String(new Error("foo"))` returns `Error: foo`. But the `Error` wrapper signals the intent better, and improves the parsing logic in `BuildBuddyError.parse`.
* Have `BuildBuddyError.parse` recognize `Error` objects and extract `error.message`, instead of relying on `String(error)` which appends an unwanted `Error: ` prefix.
* Remove error parsing in `join_org` which was duplicating the logic from `BuildBuddyError`.

author: jwodder
body:
As of Python 3.10 (released on Monday), distutils is deprecated and will be removed in Python 3.12.  As a result, using joblib under 3.10 produces deprecation warnings.  This PR fixes those warnings by replacing distutils with either [`packaging`](https://packaging.pypa.io/en/latest/) (for version comparison) or `setuptools`.

Note that, since all of the version comparisons that `LooseVersion` was used for were carried out against Python package versions, we can assume the versions in question are valid PEP 440 versions, and so `packaging.version.Version` should be used instead of the deprecated `packaging.version.LooseVersion`.

author: johnnagro
body:
This is meant to be a quick-hit fix for ENT-4980 and we'll circle back with a more "correct" fix later. The "correct" fix plan at the moment is to add a new facet to algolia which contains these "important" catalog titles for display (won't be broken up or differ between shards).

TLDR on the bug: when you query a facet which is broken up between batched/sharded records, algolia only seems to return the matching batch's version of the facet data, not the aggregated value of that facet. Fine to locate a course but not okay if your display assumes you see the aggregated value.

This quick-fix essentially keeps track of "important" catalog titles (business, education, a la carte) and ensures that every algolia batch/shard for a course always has the all the titles for "important" catalogs (not just the ones which happen to exist in that batch). I added a test which which ensures every batch contains all the important catalog titles. So, no matter which batch is returned as a result, the UI can display properly (tag courses with all the important catalogs).

- [ENT-4980](https://openedx.atlassian.net/browse/ENT-4980)

author: cameel
body:
Recently [`b_osx`](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum/solidity/19527/workflows/1cda61f8-788b-4fad-aa1a-a71e71696c04/jobs/865363) job has been failing in some of our PRs. Specifically external PRs that have been inactive for some time.

```
Failed to unarchive cache

Error untarring cache: Error extracting tarball /var/folders/1b/gl7yt7ds26vcyr1pkgld6l040000gn/T/cache3415993642 : usr/local/Homebrew/Library/Homebrew/shims/scm: Can't remove already-existing dir tar: Error exit delayed from previous errors. : exit status 1
```

["Error untarring cache" when running a macOS job](https://support.circleci.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056920051--Error-untarring-cache-when-running-a-macOS-job) suggests to include `{{ arch }}` in cache key. The reason for failures is probably that there has been an OS update after these PRs were last updated and the cache is simply no longer valid.

This PR adds `{{ arch }}` to cache keys on macOS and also on Windows just in case.

This PR updates [coverage[toml]](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **6.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- In 6.0, the coverage.py exceptions moved from coverage.misc to
  coverage.exceptions. These exceptions are not part of the public supported
  API, CoverageException is. But a number of other third-party packages were
  importing the exceptions from coverage.misc, so they are now available from
  there again (`issue 1226`_).

- Changed an internal detail of how tomli is imported, so that tomli can use
  coverage.py for their own test suite (`issue 1228`_).

- Defend against an obscure possibility under code obfuscation, where a
  function can have an argument called "self", but no local named "self"
  (`pull request 1210`_).  Thanks, Ben Carlsson.

.. _pull request 1210: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1210
.. _issue 1226: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1226
.. _issue 1228: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1228


.. _changes_60:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage html`` command now prints a message indicating where the HTML
  report was written.  Fixes `issue 1195`_.

- The ``coverage combine`` command now prints messages indicating each data
  file being combined.  Fixes `issue 1105`_.

- The HTML report now includes a sentence about skipped files due to
  ``skip_covered`` or ``skip_empty`` settings.  Fixes `issue 1163`_.

- Unrecognized options in the configuration file are no longer errors. They are
  now warnings, to ease the use of coverage across versions.  Fixes `issue
  1035`_.

- Fix handling of exceptions through context managers in Python 3.10. A missing
  exception is no longer considered a missing branch from the with statement.
  Fixes `issue 1205`_.

- Fix another rarer instance of "Error binding parameter 0 - probably
  unsupported type." (`issue 1010`_).

- Creating a directory for the coverage data file now is safer against
  conflicts when two coverage runs happen simultaneously (`pull 1220`_).
  Thanks, Clément Pit-Claudel.

.. _issue 1035: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1035
.. _issue 1105: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1105
.. _issue 1163: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1163
.. _issue 1195: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1195
.. _issue 1205: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1205
.. _pull 1220: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1220


.. _changes_60b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 2.7, PyPy 2, and Python 3.5.

- Added support for the Python 3.10 ``match/case`` syntax.

- Data collection is now thread-safe.  There may have been rare instances of
  exceptions raised in multi-threaded programs.

- Plugins (like the `Django coverage plugin`_) were generating "Already
  imported a file that will be measured" warnings about Django itself.  These
  have been fixed, closing `issue 1150`_.

- Warnings generated by coverage.py are now real Python warnings.

- Using ``--fail-under=100`` with coverage near 100% could result in the
  self-contradictory message :code:`total of 100 is less than fail-under=100`.
  This bug (`issue 1168`_) is now fixed.

- The ``COVERAGE_DEBUG_FILE`` environment variable now accepts ``stdout`` and
  ``stderr`` to write to those destinations.

- TOML parsing now uses the `tomli`_ library.

- Some minor changes to usually invisible details of the HTML report:

  - Use a modern hash algorithm when fingerprinting, for high-security
    environments (`issue 1189`_).  When generating the HTML report, we save the
    hash of the data, to avoid regenerating an unchanged HTML page. We used to
    use MD5 to generate the hash, and now use SHA-3-256.  This was never a
    security concern, but security scanners would notice the MD5 algorithm and
    raise a false alarm.

  - Change how report file names are generated, to avoid leading underscores
    (`issue 1167`_), to avoid rare file name collisions (`issue 584`_), and to
    avoid file names becoming too long (`issue 580`_).

.. _Django coverage plugin: https://pypi.org/project/django-coverage-plugin/
.. _issue 580: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/580
.. _issue 584: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/584

.. _changes_56b1:

   ```
   ----------------------------

Note: 5.6 final was never released. These changes are part of 6.0.

- Third-party packages are now ignored in coverage reporting.  This solves a
  few problems:

  - Coverage will no longer report about other people's code (`issue 876`_).
    This is true even when using ``--source=.`` with a venv in the current
    directory.

  - Coverage will no longer generate "Already imported a file that will be
    measured" warnings about coverage itself (`issue 905`_).

- The HTML report uses j/k to move up and down among the highlighted chunks of
  code.  They used to highlight the current chunk, but 5.0 broke that behavior.
  Now the highlighting is working again.

- The JSON report now includes ``percent_covered_display``, a string with the
  total percentage, rounded to the same number of decimal places as the other
  reports' totals.

Hi @rprimet, 

I did not feel comfortable with the way we supply X and D_hat to the tests. So I tried another way of supplying them via fixtures. Please check and let me know if you like it. 

Please see [this link](https://docs.pytest.org/en/latest/how-to/fixtures.html#fixtures-can-be-requested-more-than-once-per-test-return-values-are-cached) which explains that if some fixtures are called more than once in the same test, they are cached and the test function is guaranteed to have the same fixtures. So when we get X and D_hat, it is guaranteed that D_hat will be created from the same X provided in the test function.

* changement des paths de l'appli pour utiliser Univers::url * changement des roles dans le app-routing.modules.ts pour utiliser Univers:roles * seuls les modules pour lesquels l'utilisateur est autorisé sont affichés dans le header * le lien vers l'admin ne s'affiche que si l'utilisateur est autorisé dans le menu déroulant * un utilisateur 'light' est désormais stocké dans le local storage * qques corrections/refacto dans le UserDto * renommage du container 'certificate' en 'key_store' dans les fichiers properties * ajout de la clé jwt.key_store.file pour stocker le chemin vers le jks * mise à jour des variables dans le README.md * l'admin ne voit plus le lien vers le profil ## Introduction de la notion d'univers Globalement on peut considérer qu'un univers est un module (mais c'est tellement plus cool 'univers' on est d'accord ?). La liste des univers est représentée par la classe `frontend-implicaction/src/app/shared/enums/univers.ts`. Elle permet de paramétrer plusieurs éléments : * le titre associé (ex: "Offres d'emploi") * l'url (ex: jobs) * les roles utilisateurs qui sont autorisés à y accéder (ex: RoleEnumCode.USER autorise tout utilisateur connecté y compris l'admin, RoleEnumCode.ADMIN n'autorisera qu'un admin ...) * potentiellement bcp de choses pourront être paramétrés comme par exemple une palette de couleur si on met cette fonctionnalité en place de changer le "primary" en fonction du module (🍒) ## Répercution dans le code ### Au niveau du routing.module.ts il faut utiliser le tableau roles de la classe pour définir les rôles autorisé ex: ```typescript { path: Univers.ADMIN.url, loadChildren: () => import('./admin/admin.module').then(m => m.AdminModule), canActivate: [AuthGuard], data: { allowedRoles: Univers.ADMIN.roles } } ``` Vous remarquez que le ni `path` ni les `allowedRoles` ne sont écrits en dur, mais font référence à l'univers ### Au niveau des liens dans les templates on utilise dorénavant l'univers pour récupérer le path de base et on y ajoute la suite du chemin ex: ```typescript

Voir plus

``` > Les templates html ne gèrent pas encore l'appel des variables ou méthodes statiques depuis la classe (ex: `Univers.JOBS`), mais on besoin d'une instance de l'énum pour fonctionner (ex: `univers.JOBS`). Pour palier à cela, il suffit de déclarer une varibale de type univers dans le template : `univers = Univers`. Notez le `=` et non un `:`. ## Conclusion Vous pouvez voir la classe `Univers` comme un catalague de modules qui centralise tous les paramètres (routes, accès, ...). L'avantage de tout centraliser est que, si l'envie nous prend de changer un chemin, un intitulé ou des autorisation, on n'aura seulement se fichier à modifier.

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.3** to **6.0.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- In 6.0, the coverage.py exceptions moved from coverage.misc to
  coverage.exceptions. These exceptions are not part of the public supported
  API, CoverageException is. But a number of other third-party packages were
  importing the exceptions from coverage.misc, so they are now available from
  there again (`issue 1226`_).

- Changed an internal detail of how tomli is imported, so that tomli can use
  coverage.py for their own test suite (`issue 1228`_).

- Defend against an obscure possibility under code obfuscation, where a
  function can have an argument called "self", but no local named "self"
  (`pull request 1210`_).  Thanks, Ben Carlsson.

.. _pull request 1210: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1210
.. _issue 1226: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1226
.. _issue 1228: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1228


.. _changes_60:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The ``coverage html`` command now prints a message indicating where the HTML
  report was written.  Fixes `issue 1195`_.

- The ``coverage combine`` command now prints messages indicating each data
  file being combined.  Fixes `issue 1105`_.

- The HTML report now includes a sentence about skipped files due to
  ``skip_covered`` or ``skip_empty`` settings.  Fixes `issue 1163`_.

- Unrecognized options in the configuration file are no longer errors. They are
  now warnings, to ease the use of coverage across versions.  Fixes `issue
  1035`_.

- Fix handling of exceptions through context managers in Python 3.10. A missing
  exception is no longer considered a missing branch from the with statement.
  Fixes `issue 1205`_.

- Fix another rarer instance of "Error binding parameter 0 - probably
  unsupported type." (`issue 1010`_).

- Creating a directory for the coverage data file now is safer against
  conflicts when two coverage runs happen simultaneously (`pull 1220`_).
  Thanks, Clément Pit-Claudel.

.. _issue 1035: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1035
.. _issue 1105: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1105
.. _issue 1163: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1163
.. _issue 1195: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1195
.. _issue 1205: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1205
.. _pull 1220: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1220


.. _changes_60b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 2.7, PyPy 2, and Python 3.5.

- Added support for the Python 3.10 ``match/case`` syntax.

- Data collection is now thread-safe.  There may have been rare instances of
  exceptions raised in multi-threaded programs.

- Plugins (like the `Django coverage plugin`_) were generating "Already
  imported a file that will be measured" warnings about Django itself.  These
  have been fixed, closing `issue 1150`_.

- Warnings generated by coverage.py are now real Python warnings.

- Using ``--fail-under=100`` with coverage near 100% could result in the
  self-contradictory message :code:`total of 100 is less than fail-under=100`.
  This bug (`issue 1168`_) is now fixed.

- The ``COVERAGE_DEBUG_FILE`` environment variable now accepts ``stdout`` and
  ``stderr`` to write to those destinations.

- TOML parsing now uses the `tomli`_ library.

- Some minor changes to usually invisible details of the HTML report:

  - Use a modern hash algorithm when fingerprinting, for high-security
    environments (`issue 1189`_).  When generating the HTML report, we save the
    hash of the data, to avoid regenerating an unchanged HTML page. We used to
    use MD5 to generate the hash, and now use SHA-3-256.  This was never a
    security concern, but security scanners would notice the MD5 algorithm and
    raise a false alarm.

  - Change how report file names are generated, to avoid leading underscores
    (`issue 1167`_), to avoid rare file name collisions (`issue 584`_), and to
    avoid file names becoming too long (`issue 580`_).

.. _Django coverage plugin: https://pypi.org/project/django-coverage-plugin/
.. _issue 580: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/580
.. _issue 584: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/584
.. _issue 1150: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1150

.. _issue 1189: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1189
.. _tomli: https://pypi.org/project/tomli/


.. _changes_56b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.6b1
   ```
   ----------------------------

Note: 5.6 final was never released. These changes are part of 6.0.

- Third-party packages are now ignored in coverage reporting.  This solves a
  few problems:

  - Coverage will no longer report about other people's code (`issue 876`_).
    This is true even when using ``--source=.`` with a venv in the current
    directory.

  - Coverage will no longer generate "Already imported a file that will be
    measured" warnings about coverage itself (`issue 905`_).

- The HTML report uses j/k to move up and down among the highlighted chunks of
  code.  They used to highlight the current chunk, but 5.0 broke that behavior.
  Now the highlighting is working again.

- The JSON report now includes ``percent_covered_display``, a string with the
  total percentage, rounded to the same number of decimal places as the other
  reports' totals.

- ``coverage combine`` has a new option, ``--keep`` to keep the original data
  files after combining them.  The default is still to delete the files after
  they have been combined.  This was requested in `issue 1108`_ and implemented
  in `pull request 1110`_.  Thanks, Éric Larivière.

- When reporting missing branches in ``coverage report``, branches aren't
  reported that jump to missing lines.  This adds to the long-standing behavior
  of not reporting branches from missing lines.  Now branches are only reported
  if both the source and destination lines are executed.  Closes both `issue

  - It has a little more room for line numbers so that 4-digit numbers work

.. _issue 1123: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1123
.. _issue 1124: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1124

body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request! Here are some tips for you:
1. If this is your first time, check our contributor guidelines https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/about/contributing
2. To know more about Katib components, check developer guide https://github.com/kubeflow/katib/blob/master/docs/developer-guide.md
3. If you want *faster* PR reviews, check how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR fixes a bug described below.

When user edits hyper parameters' type from `'int' or 'double'` to `'Categorical' or 'Discrete'` and save the values,
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52827441/136338656-7c0d8a39-040b-4c11-9133-44e0c8e9f79e.png)

The page falls into infinite error loop.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52827441/136339874-aff4a7c2-3955-489d-9e32-5c0d38054690.png)

This bug has been caused by [this line](https://github.com/kubeflow/katib/blob/2db65b2c6b349cfd4901bfe9ee1f308f7ea6444e/pkg/new-ui/v1beta1/frontend/src/app/shared/params-list/parameter/parameter.component.ts#L85) in `parameter.component.ts`.

```typescript
this.paramCtrl
    .get('feasibleSpace')
    .setValue(group.get('feasibleSpace').value);
```

The method [setValue()](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/a92a89b0eb127a59d7e071502b5850e57618ec2d/packages/forms/src/model.ts#L1547) of `FormGroup` throws when the new value is not exactly in the same structure of the existing [FormControl](https://angular.io/api/forms/FormControl#formcontrol).

This case, the existing `Control` has already been initialized as the structure below.
(This is the difference compared to 'adding a new param'. When adding, the error does not occur.)
```typescript
{
  min: 1,
  max: 1, 
  step: ''
}
```
But the new value has a different structure as below.
```typescript
{
  list: [ '111', '222' ]
}
``` 
To replace a `Control` in a `FormGroup`, we should use the method [`setControl()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6e30b83267cdb4be62cc2c9737aeac62d14ed513/packages/forms/src/model.ts#L1322) instead of `setValue()`.

Fixes #

On some rare occasions, the project fails to compile, and swift returns a bunch of errors about `UTF8View`, saying that `Collection.SubSequence.SubSequence.Subsequence.Indices` (and so on) are not the same as `Collection.Indices`. It's pretty weird, especially since we never defined an `Indices` type on `UTF8View` so were using the default. It seems to be a canonicalisation bug; hopefully something the compiler's new requirement-machine will eliminate.

For now, work around it by defining the `Indices` type.

author: scott-taubman
body:
Closes #1055 

This PR allows the `/api/v1/requests` endpoint to accept `multipart/form-data` requests with files.  The files get converted to "base64" to facilitate transport down to a remote garden if necessary, and then the target garden will use that "base64" data to create a `RawFile` and replace the "base64" in the request parameters with an id reference to the `RawFile`.

**NOTE**: It is recognized that this is a non-optimal solution in many regards. The goal here is to get *some* means of providing files as parameter to requests targeted at remote gardens. There are many limitations here, most of which are outlined or hinted at in the description for #1055.  Memory consumption and excessively large STOMP message size are two of the big pitfalls here.  A more robust solution likely requires a redesign that's well outside the scope of this issue.  As is, files are limited to being under 100MB in size, as that's the default tornado `max_buffer_size`, which we do not set and currently provide no means of setting.

## Testing Instructions
First, you'll need to pull down [this branch](https://github.com/beer-garden/example-plugins/tree/issue/21-file-byte-example-plugin) from the example-plugins repo and make sure that the "file-bytes" plugin is loaded in your beer-garden setup.

There are UI changes required before we can use this in the UI, so instead we'll demonstrate the capability using curl.

You'll need a file to use as a test. The contents don't matter for now because we're going to task a command that just outputs the md5sum of the file.

* This tasks the `echo_md5sum` command of `file-bytes` on a garden names `parent1`:
  ```shell
  curl 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/requests' \
       -H 'accept: application/json' \
       -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data' \
       -F 'request={ "system": "file-bytes", "system_version": "1.0.0.dev0", "namespace": "parent1", 
  "command": "echo_md5sum", "comment": "", "output_type": "STRING", "instance_name": "default", 
  "parameters": {} }' \
       -F 'some_file=@/path/to/some/file'
  ```
* Do the same, replacing `parent1` with the namespace of a child garden. For extra thoroughness, do this with a child garden configured via HTTP and one via STOMP.
* In all cases, the request should succeed and the output should be the correct md5sum of the file.
* On the parent garden, viewing the request parameters in the UI should not show a mostly empty stub for the file parameter:
  ```json
  {
    "some_file": {
      "type": "bytes"
    }
  }
  ```
* On the child gardens, the file parameter should have an id field which references the RawFile object that got created:
  ```json
  {
    "some_file": {
      "type": "bytes",
      "id": "6166027ef9f07e85bcef212d"
    }
  }
  ```

This PR updates Gradle to 7.1.1 and Android Gradle Plugin to 4.2.2 which matches our major libraries & clients. Here are a few changes that were made as part of this change:
* Added plugin DSL support which is something we have been adding to all our projects
* Removes `enableUnitTestBinaryResources` from `gradle.properties` flag in d9927bdd69c0f96f2e692310107bafeae8ee8e57 which Gradle said is not supported - and didn't make a difference
* Removes unnecessary `buildToolsVersion` in fc6eb05252ac748093f024b2125d65fef414cc24 as it's now part of Android Gradle Plugin and has been stripped from our build files for other projects for some time
* Upgrades Kotlin to match current WPAndroid and fixes a couple very minor lint errors in 0b0a07d89871c2a7972fe706065e4544c0930653 - I could have upgraded the Kotlin version to the latest, but there were more lint errors and I didn't want to muddy the PR too much with Kotlin changes
* Updates Robolectric version to `4.4` which matches current WPAndroid and fixes an issue with the build f73f1f026dca0e7f8e9164d6a0412b8a861e4af3
* Updates `targetSdkVersion` to 29 - this was a necessary change to get the library building with the other changes. We probably want to upgrade it to 30 to match the latest changes in other projects. @ravishanker Could you take a look at that since you have recently worked on this? * Git ignores `.idea/compiler.xml` which is something we have done a while back for other projects

author: steveny91
body:
### What does this PR do?
A recent change in pymongo(3.11.0+) is causing the mongo check to fail if SSL is enabled and no `ssl_ca_certs` is passed in the config when running the container agent. When tested against Mongodb Atlas, this has been observed to throw an ssl_validation error.  This change is aimed at trying to load CA certs from certifi if SSL is enabled and `ssl_ca_certs` is not configured in the config. 

### Motivation
From support ticket

### Additional Notes
I'm suspecting that with the inclusion of pyopenssl in pymongo(3.11.0), the default location in which pymongo loads these CA certs are no longer the same or it's not being loaded at all. 


### Review checklist (to be filled by reviewers)

- [ ] Feature or bugfix MUST have appropriate tests (unit, integration, e2e)
- [ ] PR title must be written as a CHANGELOG entry [(see why)](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-title)

disable-group=True

author: kirbyquerby
body:
When using the error reporting API to report errors, labels are lost in the resulting logs as there's no field for them. However, errors can also be sent to error reporting via the logging API, as per https://cloud.google.com/error-reporting/docs/formatting-error-messages

This change adds an Option UseLoggingServiceForErrors which allows errors to be reported to error reporting via the logging API rather than the error reporting API, preserving any attached labels.

author: ipeterov
body:
Looks like this topic is not covered well in documentation - I had to wander around in code to figure out how to add a UIDField to an existing model.

Not sure if the suggested method is the best - I thought of another alternative option:
```
from django_uidfield import new_uid

def populate_uid(apps, schema_editor):
    User = apps.get_model("users", "User")

    for user in User.objects.all():
        user.uid = new_uid(20, prefix="usr_")
        user.save()


class Migration(migrations.Migration):

    operations = [migrations.RunPython(code=populate_uid)]
```

^ This is probably a bit easier to understand, but you have to repeat the same settings that you specified in the field.

body:
Customization of the iFrame. The theme may now supply its version of the html

getAlbumThumbImage() will always return an image, removed the if test. (The default image is returned if there is no other choice.)

Documented rewrite URLs and how to customize the iFrame

Fixed discrepancy between the query and the rewrite rule. The iFrame rewrite rule used "oembed" while the query parameter used "embed". Rule is changed to "embed". Added handling of root URLs.

The lines $iframe = str_replace(array('\r', '\n'), '', $iframe); did not do anything as the representation for end-of-line is double quote, not single quote. Besides there is miniscule file size savings for removing the end of line characters and it makes looking at the HTML output messy, thus impacting debugging.

Use npg icon as default

Add display of errors for iFrames

author: soulitzer
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack):
* #68629
* #68628
* #67045
* #67041
* #67820
* #66294
* #66293
* __->__ #66292

In this PR:
1. Fix the case when tangent has a different layout from the base when `set_fw_grad` by adding a native function and its batching rule.

For (1) we replace the following:
```
Tensor new_with_same_meta(const Variable& base) {
  int64_t nelement_in_storage = base.storage().nbytes() / base.itemsize();
  auto new_tensor = at::zeros({nelement_in_storage}, base.options());
  auto res = new_tensor.as_strided(base.sizes(), base.strides(), base.storage_offset());
  return res;
}
```
with a native function as to enable a batching rule to alter its behavior.

This new function will be similar to `new_zeros_strided` except we also require the `storage_offset` and `storage_numel` arguments.

Possible concerns:
 - Why have redundant logic? Why not add new args `new_zeros_strided`? This is probably a niche use case, so it's better not to complicate the current API.
 - Previously the created tensor inherits the TensorOptions of the primal. Now we inherit from the TensorOptions of the tangent.
   - Probably fine. Likely, no one relies on this because the behavior is only triggered when tangent/base have different layouts.
 - Why pass in exploded size, stride, and offset? It is possible in the non-batched case to pass in a tensor directly, but not possible when we'd like to have a batching rule. The size, stride, and offset we'd be passing won't belong to any live tensor.

This PR:
 - Asserts that if the output is a view, then the `is_same_metadata` must return `true`. Otherwise, we are performing a copy. 
 - unless we are being called from `make_dual` which can allow the tangent and primal to have different layouts, because it is not forward differentiable.
 - To make this possible, we add `is_make_dual` as a parameter. ~The alternative is to make `make_dual` non-composite, and then we can rely on its `view_info` for differentiability information. This also assumes that the only composite function that calls `set_fw_grad` is `make_dual`.~
 - Batching rules now preserve storage offset for view operator that return non-zero storage offset

author: marip8
body:
I have a use case where I would like to use the `docker` image produced by ICI to be the base image and `UNDERLAY` for CI for a different repository. This is problematic because the current names of the workspaces built by ICI are hard-coded to `base_ws`, `upstream_ws`, `target_ws`, and `downstream_ws`. This means that I need to specify `UNDERLAY=/root/target_ws/install`, but the source code of the second repository also gets copied into `/root/target_ws/src`. Coincidentally this works for simple repositories, but (probably) breaks down if an upstream workspace is needed for the second repository build.

The proposed fix to this issue is to prepend the name of the target repository to each workspace name. For example `target_ws` for `repo_a` would become `repo_a_target_ws`. Then `repo_b` could use `UNDERLAY=/root/repo_a_target_ws/install`, and its own upstream and target workspaces would be built in `/root/repo_b_upstream_ws` and `/root_repo_b_target_ws`, respectively, producing the desired workspace chain

body:
## Description

This pr both adds an `endgame_mac` keymap and fixes the `endgame` keymap. 

Changes introduced in #12097 (4b96d5876eb01dfd8063949a2e5cb4b70e01786d) actually broke the endgame keymap as the function `md_rgb_matrix_indicators` was replaced with `md_rgb_matrix_indicators_advanced`. body:
Fixes #1704

This PR ensures that `CRubyBuffer` continuously tries to maintain the internal buffer to less then `@max_size` items.

This is done by "clamping" the internal array to `@max_size` when we detect at any point that the buffer is full. This eventually catches any race modifications that would cause the buffer to exceed its maximum size.

body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

_What is this about?_
This PR is intended to introduce functionality to the deploy.py file that requires nsg-rules during deployment. 
In addition, I've refactored much of the set_admins code into a more general configuration.py file that acts as a new library of instance_config-based functionality. The nsg_rule update functionality has been included in this file. 

## PR Checklist
* [x] Applies to work item: #1316
* [ ] ~CLA signed. If not, go over [here](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com/microsoft/onefuzz) and sign the CLI.~
* [ ] ~Tests added/passed~
* [ ] ~Requires documentation to be updated~
* [x] I've discussed this with core contributors already. If not checked, I'm ready to accept this work might be rejected in favor of a different grand plan. Issue number where discussion took place: #xxx

## Info on Pull Request

_What does this include?_
Changes to deploy.py: 
* New required param (nsg_config) that takes in a list of IPs to act as a default IP allow list. 
* New file, configuration.py, that includes code from set_admins.py that deals with instance_config updates. Also includes nsg_config update functions
* Removed instance_config functions from set_admins.py

## Validation Steps Performed
Deploying test build and testing value config. 

_How does someone test & validate?_
More specifically, to test and validate this work, I am downloading the 'custom' release-artifacts from the below build and deploying them to my subscription. I then test the following using the 'custom' CLI from release-artifiacts: 
* [ ] Run >onefuzz instance_config update @C:\body.json where body.json includes a list of individual IPs and IP ranges
* [ ] Run >onefuzz instance_config update @C:\body.json where body.json includes updated list of service tags
* [ ] Upgraded (not just new) instances work, as specified by the existing test checklist
